title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is the continuation of §B ('cas des surfaces ponctuées', i.e. punctured surfaces) of the sequel to La Longue Marche. The previous page introduced a category Rev(S) of étale coverings for a germ of space S, defined the universal coverings of S as its 1-connected objects, and gave an isomorphism π1(S,S̃) ≅ Aut(S̃).

On this page Grothendieck specialises to the setting of (53): X is a topological space and x ∈ X a point where X is a surface (a topological 2-manifold near x).

1. He forms the 'punctured germ' D_x^*. This is the pro-object, or germ, given by the system of punctured discs D_{x,i}^* = D_{x,i} \ {x}, where the D_{x,i} run over a basis of disc neighbourhoods of x.

2. Its covering category is a direct 2-limit: Rev(D_x^*) = 2-colim_i Rev(D_{x,i}^*).
   - Each Rev(D_{x,i}^*) is Galois with π1 ≅ Z.
   - The restriction maps are equivalences, because the π1 of the punctured discs form an essentially constant projective system.
   - Hence Rev(D_x^*) is an ordinary Galois category (connected, not merely multigaloisienne).

3. Its fundamental group is identified canonically with the orientation module T_x of X at x (a free Z-module of rank 1, ≅ H_1(D^*) ≅ H^2_x(X,Z)^∨, up to convention). This is (56): π1(D_x^*) := π1(Rev(D_x^*)) ≅ T_x.
   - The identification is canonical and needs no base point, because the group is abelian.
   - Consequently the universal coverings D̃_x^* form a connected groupoid whose automorphism group is T_x. The image reads 'de groupe fondamental T_x'.

4. He then fixes one such D̃_x^* and begins to consider the composite D̃_x^* → D_x^* ↪ X − {x}. The next page generalises this to U = X \ S and uses the composite to define a fundamental group π1(U, D̃_x^*) based at the punctured germ.

5. The purpose is a canonical homomorphism K_x : T_x → π1(U, D̃_x^*). This is the local monodromy (inertia) at the puncture, with a universal cover of the punctured germ serving as a 'tangential' base point. It is the topological prototype of the base-point system Grothendieck needs for the Teichmüller tower and for Galois actions on π1 of punctured curves.
errors: No mathematical error. The 'canonique' identification π1 ≅ T_x depends on a convention for the orientation module (H_1 of the punctured disc versus local cohomology). This is harmless.
The essential constancy of π1 of the punctured discs D_{x,i}^* requires the D_{x,i} to be actual discs, i.e. the surface hypothesis at x. This is given.

ideas.what: The fundamental group / Galois category of the punctured germ at a point of a surface, computed as a 2-colimit over punctured disc neighbourhoods
ideas.modern_name: Local fundamental group of a punctured neighbourhood (inertia group at a puncture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (topology); algebraic analogue: SGA1 / Grothendieck–Murre tame fundamental group
ideas.where_published: Germs of this kind in étale theory appear in SGA1/SGA2; this topological germ formalism is in the unpublished Longue Marche sequel

ideas.what: Canonical identification of π1 of the punctured germ with the orientation module T_x
ideas.modern_name: Local orientation / canonical generator of inertia, Z(1)-type twist
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical; the Z(1) viewpoint goes back to Grothendieck (SGA4, SGA5)
ideas.where_published: Orientation modules / Z(1) in SGA4 and SGA5; T_x in the Longue Marche

ideas.what: Using a universal covering of the punctured germ as a base point for π1(U), giving a canonical map T_x → π1(U, D̃_x^*)
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base point (base point at a puncture) and the local monodromy map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989, 'Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points'); also Anderson–Ihara
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) alludes to systems of base points; La Longue Marche (1981, partially edited by Malgoire) uses base points attached to punctures

missed.claim: A worked-out topological formalism of tangential base points via universal coverings of punctured germs (Galois categories of germs) appears in Grothendieck's 1981 notes, predating Deligne's 1989 tangential base points. Specialists know Grothendieck used base points at punctures, but this precise germ-theoretic definition sits in the unedited part of the Longue Marche.
missed.quote: Ainsi les rev. universels D̃_x^* de D_x^* forment un groupoïde connexe, de groupe fondamental T_x. Choisissons donc un tel D̃_x^*
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents priority and a clean base-point-free, groupoid-theoretic formulation of tangential base points and inertia. This is relevant to the history of anabelian geometry and to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller formalism.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard. The interest is historical: an explicit 1981 germ-theoretic construction of tangential base points and inertia maps, in an unpublished part of the Longue Marche. Grothendieck's use of such base points is broadly known, so this is a modest detail.

'de groupoïde fondamental [-Ex-] T_x' should read 'de groupe fondamental T_x'.
The margin reads 'B) Cas des surfaces ponctuées' (the second word is plausibly 'ponctuées').
The struck-out heading at the top appears to be '[-Rem-]' followed by 'F.'.
